about: Read-only cross-check of the module's at-Taysir claims against Marijn van Putten's translation (CC BY-NC 4.0). Not evidence for any claim.

categories.statement_on_verse_pages_agree: van Putten translates a statement on the claim's verse, on the page the claim cites (within one page).
categories.cites_the_suras_closing_list: The claim cites a page of the sura's closing yāʾ list, which he translates without verse numbers.
categories.cites_a_general_principle: The claim cites a page of the uṣūl, the general principles.
categories.cites_an_earlier_page_not_word_checked: The claim cites an earlier page that carries a translated statement, as a rule stated once where a word first occurs would. That the statement concerns this word is not checked here.
categories.statement_on_verse_pages_differ: He translates a statement on the verse, but the claim cites a later page: review.
categories.no_statement_on_verse: He has no statement on the verse and the cited page carries none: review.

Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read bi-mā kasabat without fāʾ and the rest read fa-bi-mā with fāʾ.[359]
Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read yaʿlamu llaḏīna with rafʿ of the mīm and the rest with naṣb (i.e., yaʿlama).

Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read kabīra l-ʾiṯmi here and in al-Naǧm (Q53:32) with kasrah on the bāʾ without ʾalif or hamzah. The rest read it with fatḥah on the bāʾ, and with ʾalif and hamzah after it (i.e., kabāʾira).
Nāfiʿ reads ʾaw yursilu with rafʿ of the lām and fa-yūḥī bi-ʾiḏnihī with no vowel on the yāʾ. The rest read both with naṣb (i.e., yursila, fa-yūḥiya).
Nāfiʿ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ṣafḥan ʾin kuntum with kasrah on the hamzah and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., ʾan).

Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾa-wa-man yunaššaʾu with ḍammah on the yāʾ, fatḥah on the nūn and gemination of the šīn. The rest read it with fatḥah on the yāʾ, no vowel on the nūn and no gemination of the šīn (i.e., yanšaʾu).

The two of the holy cities and Ibn ʿĀmir read ʿinda r-raḥmāni with a nūn that does not carry a vowel and with fatḥah on the dāl. The rest read it with a bāʾ that carries a fatḥah, with ʾalif after it and with ḍammah on the dāl (i.e., ʿibādu
Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read qāla ʾulū with an ʾalif and the rest read qul without ʾalif.
Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read saqfan with fatḥah on the sīn and without a vowel on the qāf as a singular. The rest read it with ḍammah on both as a plural (i.e., suqufan).
ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah and Hišām, with some disagreement, here read lammā matāʿu with gemination of the mīm and the rest read it without gemination (i.e., la-mā).
The two of the holy cities, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū Bakr read ʾiḏā ǧāʾānā with ʾalif as a dual, and the rest read it without ʾalif as a singular (i.e., ǧāʾanā).
Ḥafṣ reads ʿalayhi ʾaswiratun without a vowel on the sīn and without ʾalif. The rest read it with fatḥah on it and with ʾalif after it (i.e., ʾasāwiratun).
Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read fa-ǧaʿalnāhum sulufan with ḍammah on both the sīn and the lām. The rest read it with fatḥah on both (i.e., salafan).
Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read yaṣuddūna with ḍammah on the ṣād and the rest read it with kasrah (i.e., yaṣiddūna).

The Kufans read ʾa-ʾālihatunā ḫayrun with full pronunciation of the two hamzahs and with an ʾalif after it. The rest read it with softening of the second (hamzah) and with ʾalif after it (i.e., ʾa-.ālihatunā). None of them introduces an ʾal
Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read taštahīhi l-ʾanfusu with two hāʾs and the rest read it with one (i.e., taštahī).[367]
Ibn Kaṯīr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-ʾilayhi yurǧaʿūna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ.
ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read waqīlihī with ḫafḍ of the lām and with kasrah on the hāʾ. The rest read it with naṣb of the lām and with ḍammah on the hāʾ (i.e., waqīlahū).
Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read fa-sawfa taʿmalūna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaʿmalūna).
The Kufans read rabbi s-samāwāti with ḫafḍ and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., rabbu).
Ibn Kaṯīr and Ḥafṣ read yaġlī fì l-buṭūni with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taġlī).
The two of the holy cities and Ibn ʿĀmir read fa-ʿtulūhu with ḍammah on the tāʾ and the rest with kasrah (i.e., fa-ʿtilūhu).
Al-Kisāʾī reads ḏuq ʾannaka with fatḥah on the hamzah and the rest with kasrah (i.e., ʾinnaka).
Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read fī muqāmin with ḍammah on the mīm and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., maqāmin).

Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read taṣrīfi r-rīḥi ʾāyātin (Q45:5) and min dābbatin ʾāyātin (Q45:4) with ar-rīḥi in the singular and with kasrah on the tāʾ of both words. The rest read it in the plural and with rafʿ of the tāʾ (i.e., taṣrīfi r-riyāḥi
Ibn ʿĀmir, ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī wa-ʾāyātihī tuʾimūna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yuʾ/ūminūna).
min riǧzin ʾalīmu/in has already been mentioned.[370]
ʾAbū ʿAmr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read li-naǧziya qawman with nūn and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaǧziya).
Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read sawāʾan maḥyā/ēhum with naṣb and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., sawāʾun).
Ḥamzah reads wa-s-sāʿata lā rayba fīhā with naṣb and the rest with rafʿ.
lā yuḫraǧūna/yaḫruǧūna has already been mentioned.[371] There are no yāʾs at all.
Nāfiʿ, al-Bazzī, with some disagreement, and Ibn ʿĀmir read li-tunḏira llaḏīna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., li-yunḏira).

The Kufans read bi-wālidayhi ʾiḥsānan with a hamzah that carries a kasrah, without vowel on the ḥāʾ, with fatḥah on the sīn and with an ʾalif after it. The rest read ḥusnan with ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and no vowel on the sīn without ʾalif.[372]

Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read nataqabbalu ʿanhum ʾaḥsana mā ʿamilū wa-nataǧāwazu with nūn on both, with both carrying a fatḥah and with naṣb of the nūn of ʾaḥsana. The rest read it with yāʾ that carries a ḍammah on both words and with raf
Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and Hišām read wa-li-yuwaffiyahum(ū) with yāʾ and the rest read it with nūn (i.e., wa-li-nuwaffiyahum).

Ibn Ḏakwān reads ʾa-ʾaḏhabtum with two fully pronounced hamzahs without length. Ibn Kaṯīr and Hišām read it with hamzah and length, and Hišām stretches it in terms of length (i.e., Ibn Kaṯīr ʾa-.aḏhabtumū, Hišām ʾā-.aḏhabtum) according to h

ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read lā yurā/ē with a yāʾ that carries a ḍammah and ʾillā masākinuhum with rafʿ. The rest read it with a tāʾ that carries a fatḥah and with naṣb (i.e., lā yarā/ē/ǟ ʾillā masākinahum(ū)).
Ḥafṣ and ʾAbū ʿAmr read wa-llaḏīna qutilū with ḍammah on the qāf and kasrah on the tāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on both, with an ʾalif between them (i.e., qātalū).
Ibn Kaṯīr reads ʾasinin with shortness and the rest with length (i.e., ʾāsinin).

Muḥammad b. ʾAḥmad b. ʿAlī al-Baġdādī related to us, saying that Ibn Muǧāhid related to us, saying that Muḍar b. Muḥammad related to us from al-Bazzī with his ʾisnād back to Ibn Kaṯīr that he said ʾanifan with shortness, and this is how I r
ʾAbū ʿAmr recites wa-ʾumliya lahum with ḍammah on the hamzah, kasrah on the lām and fatḥah on the yāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on the hamzah and the lām (i.e., wa-ʾamlā/ē/ǟ).
Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾisrārahum with kasrah on the hamzah and the rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., ʾasrārahum(ū)).
ʾAbū Bakr reads wa-li-yabluwannakum ḥattā yaʿlama and yabluwa with yāʾ for all three; the rest read them with nūn (i.e., wa-li-nabluwannakum(ū) ḥattā naʿlama, nabluwa).
ʾAbū Bakr and Ḥamzah said wa-tadʿū ʾilà s-silmi with kasrah on the sīn and the rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., as-salmi).

Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read li-yuʾ/ūminū bi-llāhi wa-rasūlihī wa-yuʿazzirūhu wa-yuwaqqirūhu wa-yusabbiḥūhu with yāʾ in all four and the rest read them with tāʾ (i.e., li-tuʾ/ūminū bi-llāhi wa-rasūlihī wa-tuʿazzirūhu wa-tuwaqqirūhu wa-tusab
Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read bikum ḍurran with ḍammah on the ḍād and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., ḍarran).
Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read kalima ḷḷāhi with kasrah on the lām; the rest read it with fatḥah and an ʾalif after it (i.e., kalāma).
Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read nudḫilhu and nuʿaḏḏibhu with nūn on both. The rest read them with yāʾ (i.e., yudḫilhū̆, yuʿaḏḏibhū̆).
ʾAbū ʿAmr reads bimā yaʿlamūna baṣīran with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taʿlamūna).

Ibn Kaṯīr and Ibn Ḏakwān read šaṭaʾahū with vowel on the ṭāʾ and the rest without a vowel (i.e., šaṭʾahū). Ibn Ḏakwān reads fa-ʾazarahū with shortness and the rest with length (i.e., fa-ʾāzarahū). ʿalā suʾqihī/suʾūqihī/sūqihī has already be
fa-taṯabbatū/fa-tabayyanū,[382] laḥma ʾaḫīhī̆ may(yi)tan (Q49:12)[383] and the tāʾs of al-Bazzī (Q49:11, 12, 13)[384] have already been mentioned before.
ʾAbū ʿAmr reads yaʾlitkum with hamzah without a vowel after the yāʾ and, when he softens it, he replaces it with ʾalif (i.e., yālitkum). The rest read it without hamzah or ʾalif (i.e., yalitkum(ū)).
Ibn Kaṯīr reads baṣīrun bimā yaʿlamūna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taʿlamūna).
Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū Bakr read yawma yaqūlu with yāʾ and the rest read it with nūn (i.e., naqūlu).
Ibn Kaṯīr reads hāḏā mā yūʿadūna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tūʿadūna).
The two of the holy cities and Ḥamzah read wa-ʾidbāra s-suǧūdi with kasrah on the hamzah and the rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., wa-ʾadbāra).
ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read miṯlu mā ʾannakum with rafʿ of the lām and the rest with naṣb (i.e., miṯla).
[388] Al-Kisāʾī reads fa-ʾaḫaḏathumu ṣ-ṣaʿqatun without a vowel on the ʿayn and without ʾalif. The rest read it with ʾalif and kasrah on the ʿayn (i.e., ṣ-ṣāʿiqatun).
ʾAbū ʿAmr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-qawmi nūḥin with ḫafḍ and the rest with naṣb (i.e., wa-qawma).

ʾAbū ʿAmr reads wa-ʾatbaʿnāhum with ʾalif al-qaṭʿ and without a vowel on both the tāʾ and the ʿayn, and with nūn and an ʾalif after the nūn. The rest read it with ʾalif al-waṣl with fatḥah on both the tāʾ and the ʿayn, and with tāʾ without
Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read ʾannahū huwa l-barru with fatḥah on the hamzah and the rest with kasrah (i.e., ʾinnahū).

Qunbul, Ḥafṣ, with some disagreement, and Hišām read al-musayṭirūna with sīn. Ḥamzah, with disagreement in the transmission of Ḫallād, reads it between the ṣād and the zāy (i.e., al-muẓayṭirūna). The rest read it with pure ṣād (i.e., al-muṣ
ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read fīhi yuṣʿaqūna with ḍammah on the yāʾ and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., yaṣʿaqūna).

Hišām reads mā kaḏḏaba l-fuʾādu with gemination of the ḏāl and the rest without gemination (i.e., kaḏaba).

Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾa-fa-tamrūnahū with fatḥah on the tāʾ and without a vowel on the mīm. The rest read it with ḍammah on the tāʾ, fatḥah on the mīm and with ʾalif after it (i.e., ʾa-fa-tumārūnahū).
Ibn Kaṯīr reads wa-manâʾata with length and hamzah. The rest read it without length and without hamzah (i.e., wa-manāta).
Ibn Kaṯīr reads wa-ḍiʾzā with hamzah and the rest without hamzah (i.e., wa-ḍīzā/ē/ǟ).

Ibn Kaṯīr reads ʾilā šayʾin nukrin with no vowel on the kāf and the rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., nukurin).

ʾAbū ʿAmr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ḫāšiʿan with fatḥah on the ḫāʾ, with ʾalif after it and with kasrah on the šīn. The rest read it with ḍammah on the ḫāʾ and fatḥah on a geminate šīn (i.e., ḫuššaʿan).
Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamzah read sa-taʿlamūna ġadan with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., sa-yaʿlamūna).

Ibn ʿĀmir reads wa-l-ḥabba ḏà l-ʿaṣfi wa-r-rayḥāna with naṣb of the three nouns. Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-r-rayḥāni with ḫafḍ and what remains with rafʿ (i.e., wa-l-ḥabbu ḏù l-ʿaṣfi wa-r-rayḥāni). The rest read all three with rafʿ (i.e.
Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr read yuḫraǧu minhumā with ḍammah on the yāʾ and fatḥah on the rāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on the yāʾ and ḍammah on the rāʾ (i.e., yaḫruǧu).
Ḥamzah and ʾAbū Bakr, with some disagreement, read al-munšiʾātu with kasrah on the šīn, and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., al-munšaʾātu).[396]
Ibn Kaṯīr reads šiwāḏ̣un with kasrah on the šīn and the rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., šuwāḏ̣un). Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read wa-nuḥāsin with ḫafḍ, and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., wa-nuḥāsun).

Ibn ʿĀmir reads ḏù l-ǧalāli at the end (i.e., as opposed to the one at Q55:27) with wāw and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., ḏì l-ǧalāli).[399]
The Kufans read wa-lā yunzifūna with kasrah on the zāy and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., yunzafūna).
Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-ḥūrin ʿīnin with ḫafḍ of both and the rest read it with rafʿ of both (i.e., wa-ḥūrun ʿīnun).
ʾAbū Bakr and Ḥamzah read ʿurban with no vowel on the rāʾ and the rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., ʿuruban).

Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read šurba l-hīmi with ḍammah on the šīn and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., šarba).
Ibn Kaṯīr reads naḥnu qadarnā without gemination of the dāl and the rest with gemination (i.e., qaddarnā).
ʾAbū Bakr reads ʾaʾinnā la-muġrimūna with two hamzahs and the rest with a single hamzah that carries a kasrah (i.e., ʾinnā).

ʾAbū ʿAmr reads wa-qad ʾuḫiḏa with ḍammah on the hamzah, kasrah on the ḫāʾ, and mīṯāqukum with rafʿ. The rest read it with fatḥah on the hamzah, with ḫāʾ and with naṣb (i.e., wa-qad ʾaḫaḏā mīṯāqakum(ū)).
Ibn ʿĀmir reads wa-kullun waʿada ḷḷāhu with rafʿ. The rest read it with naṣb (i.e., kullan).[403]

Ḥamzah reads li-llaḏīna ʾāmanū ʾanḏ̣irūnā with hamzat al-qaṭʿ and fatḥah both when starting on it and in connected speech (fì l-ḥālayn), and kasrah on the ḏ̣āʾ. The rest read it with ʾalif al-waṣl and, if they start on it, with ḍammah and w
Ibn ʿĀmir reads lā tuʾḫaḏu with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yuʾ/ūḫaḏu).

Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū Bakr read al-muṣaddaqīna wa-l-muṣaddaqāti without gemination of the ṣād of both and the rest read them with gemination of both (i.e., al-muṣṣaddaqīna wa-l-muṣṣaddaqāti).
ʾAbū ʿAmr reads bi-mā ʾatākum with shortness and the rest with length (i.e., ʾātā/ē/ǟkum(ū)).

Ibn Kaṯīr, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read mutimmu without tanwīn and nūrihī with ḫafḍ. The rest read it with tanwīn and naṣb (i.e., mutimmun nūrahū).
Ibn ʿĀmir reads tunaǧǧīkum with gemination and the rest without gemination (i.e., tunǧīkum(ū)).
